subject.title: fix: stop doctor misreporting trusted-proxy gateways as unauthenticated

question: Should Doctor downgrade an exposed Gateway from unauthenticated CRITICAL to trusted-proxy WARNING when startup-valid trusted-proxy auth is configured, while retaining firewall guidance and criticals for every invalid or unsafe boundary?
rationale: The patch is designed to mirror runtime acceptance, but whether that complete configuration should count as sufficient auth proof for a security diagnostic is an intentional operator-security policy choice rather than a mechanical correctness question.

options.title: Accept runtime-valid trusted-proxy proof
options.body: Approve the guarded WARNING classification once current-head live proof confirms the default Doctor path does not execute exec SecretRef providers.

options.title: Keep the generic critical
options.body: Retain the existing unauthenticated CRITICAL for every exposed trusted-proxy deployment and narrow this PR to remediation wording only.

options.title: Split policy from implementation
options.body: Keep the fail-closed helper but pause this PR until owners define the intended severity and remediation contract in the Doctor security policy.

recommendation.title: Accept runtime-valid trusted-proxy proof
recommendation.body: Approve the guarded WARNING classification once current-head live proof confirms the default Doctor path does not execute exec SecretRef providers.

likelyOwner.reason: Their trusted-proxy auth hardening work most directly defines the source and authorization invariant this diagnostic is intended to mirror.
